key_insight: AI-assisted mammography reading reduced follow-up assessments and recalls in routine screening, while cancer detection stayed essentially unchanged.
clinical_relevance: In real-world breast cancer screening, AI may improve workflow efficiency and specificity without clearly changing detection rates.
method: Retrospective comparison of one Czech screening unit in 2022 (no AI) vs 2023 (AI used)
Women aged 45–69 were included from the Breast Cancer Screening Registry
Adjusted analyses used chi-square tests and logistic regression controlling for age, risk level, and screening round
evidence_signal: In 4,034 non-AI and 4,049 AI-assisted exams, FAR fell from 5.2% to 3.9% and RR from 2.4% to 1.9%, while CDR changed from 5.0 to 5.2 per 1,000 women.
watch_item: This was a single-center retrospective study across two different years, so results may reflect local practice changes and may not generalize widely.
paper_title: Impact of AI-Assisted Mammography Reading on Quality Indicators in the Czech Breast Cancer Screening Programme: A Retrospective Study
